'''''Cornus alba''''', the '''red-barked, white''' or '''Siberian dogwood''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Cornaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to [[Siberia]], northern [[China]] and [[Korea]]. It is a large [[deciduous]] [[basal shoot|surculose]] (suckering) shrub that can be grown as a small tree. As a popular ornamental used in landscaping its notable features include the red stems in fall (autumn) through late winter, bright winter bark;<ref>[[Donald Wyman]], ''Wyman's Garden Encyclopedia'', ''s.v." Cornus alba 'Sibirica' "''.</ref> and the [[variegated]] foliage in some [[cultivar]]s, such as ''C. alba'' 'Elegantissima'. ''C. alba'' can grow to {{convert|3|m|0|abbr=on}} high, but variegated forms are less vigorous. For the brightest winter bark, young shoots are encouraged by cutting to the ground some older stems at the end of the winter, before leaves are open. The oval fruits are white, sometimes tinted blue.<ref name=AZEGP>{{cite book
| editor-last = Brickell
| editor-first = Christopher
| title = The Royal Horticultural Society A-Z Encyclopedia of Garden Plants
| year = 2008
| page = 306
| publisher = Dorling Kindersley
| location = United Kingdom
| isbn = 9781405332965}}</ref>

The plant is extremely hardy, to [[USDA Zone]] 3 - {{convert|-40|C|F|abbr=on}}.

The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''alba'' means “white”.<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for Gardeners |year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=978-1845337315 }}</ref>

The following cultivars have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]] (confirmed 2017):-<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 22 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 24 January 2018}}</ref> 
*'Aurea'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Cornus alba'' 'Aurea'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/99361/Cornus-alba-Aurea/Details | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref> (yellow leaves)
*'Elegantissima'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Cornus alba'' 'Elegantissima'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/89376/Cornus-alba-Elegantissima-(v)/Details | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref> (deep red stems and small white flowers)
*'Sibirica'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Cornus alba'' 'Sibirica'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/99959/Cornus-alba-Sibirica/Details | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref> ({{convert|2.5|m|0|abbr=on}}, brilliant red stems, cream flowers)
*'Spaethii'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Cornus alba'' 'Spaethii'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/92514/Cornus-alba-Spaethii-(v)/Details | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref> (variegated leaves with yellow margins)
